Shorten injection 5's gradient while keeping its solvent window and temperature fixed to test whether the critical pair responds to slope. This should bring the last peak close to 10 minutes while preserving retention of the early peaks and ensuring complete elution.

Keep injection 9's gradient fixed and raise temperature to shift selectivity at the sole unresolved pair, which responded only weakly to gradient duration. The higher temperature should also keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test the midpoint temperature to balance the two critical separations: 60 C improved the late cluster but nearly merged an earlier pair. At 55 C, both may exceed R = 1.5 while the last peak remains below 10 minutes.

Injection 11 reached the maximum CRF; shorten its gradient by one grid step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep temperature and solvent endpoints fixed to test whether the critical pairs retain R ≥ 1.5.

Keep injection 11 as the maximum-score benchmark and test a cooler selectivity regime with the shorter gradient. Cooling beyond the near-coelution seen at 50 C may separate that pair in the opposite order while improving the pair that limited injection 12.

Test a narrower solvent window at the shorter gradient duration to recover the critical separation lost in injection 12. Raising phi0 also tests whether the early pair retains sufficient resolution while shortening overall elution.

Lower the starting organic fraction from injection 12 to improve the critical early-middle separation, since raising it in injection 14 made that pair worse. This tests whether the 10-minute gradient can achieve full resolution while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes.

Shorten injection 15's gradient by one grid step to test for a faster maximum-score method. Keep the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed so the result directly shows whether the two critical pairs tolerate further compression.

Narrow the gradient window to restore resolution of the slope-sensitive pair while retaining the 8-minute gradient. The last peak's estimated elution fraction is about 0.57 in injection 15, so an endpoint of 0.60 should still allow prompt complete elution.

Test a cooler selectivity regime for a faster fully resolved method, retaining injection 17 as the maximum-score benchmark. Relative to injection 13, cooling may separate its critical pair further, while the shorter gradient offsets the increased retention.

Shift injection 16's solvent window downward while keeping its slope and temperature fixed, aiming to improve the limiting separation through stronger initial retention. This tests for full resolution at a faster elution time than injection 17, while monitoring the other close pair.

Test whether a steeper gradient at 60 C separates the earlier critical pair on the opposite side of its apparent elution-order crossover. Injection 19 remains the fastest maximum-score benchmark; this run explores a potentially faster selectivity regime.

The critical pair at 60 C appears to separate after an elution-order crossover as the gradient steepens. Test a 4-minute gradient to seek R ≥ 1.5 on that side of the crossover, while checking that neighboring pairs remain resolved.

Return to the nearly resolved 40 C regime of injection 13, lowering phi0 to shift selectivity while shortening the gradient to reduce elution time. This tests another route to a faster maximum-score method, with injection 19 retained as the fastest fully resolved benchmark.

Increase injection 19's endpoint by one grid step to test the speed limit of the fastest fully resolved method. Both critical pairs have little resolution margin, so retain injection 19 if this modest steepening drops either below R = 1.5.

Test a gradient slope between injections 16 and 17, aiming to preserve full resolution with a last peak slightly earlier than injection 17. This may offer more resolution margin than injection 19 while retaining the maximum CRF.

Use the final injection to test whether a higher starting organic fraction and narrower window improve the critical separation in the 40 C regime while shortening elution. Injection 19 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, already achieving the maximum CRF.
